summary: Implementation provides robust support for gradual typing via hole variables. Correctly distinguishes anonymous holes (fresh constraints) from named holes (consistency enforced).

correctness.hole_identity: hole->var correctly maps (? x) to consistent symbols (?x) and ? to fresh symbols (?1, ?2)
correctness.unification: unify-with correctly handles hole-with-hole and hole-with-type cases, preserving most specific information
correctness.occurs_check: occurs? correctly prevents infinite types involving hole variables
correctness.generalization: Hole variables correctly excluded from generalization - free-tvars does not recognize ?-prefixed symbols as type variables

forall_types.note: Naive structural equality for ∀ types - no alpha-renaming. (∀ (a) a) will not unify with (∀ (b) b)
forall_types.impact: Unifying (∀ (a) (? x)) with (∀ (a) Int) works, but bound variable matching is fragile

recursive_types.note: μ types unified structurally - no unfolding or alpha-equivalence of recursive binders

naming_collisions.note: Symbols starting with ? are treated as hole variables - user-defined ?T would be misinterpreted

included: hole->var - convert holes to hole variables
missing: Finalization/defaulting pass to convert unconstrained holes to Dynamic/Any type

performance.concern: Substitution uses association lists (assq) with O(N) lookup
performance.impact: Could become bottleneck for large inference contexts with many holes
performance.recommendation: Consider hash map or balanced tree for Subst if performance degrades

gaps: No explicit tests for holes nested within ∀ or μ types (though static analysis suggests apply-subst handles them correctly)

conclusion: Implementation is logically sound and fits well into the existing bidirectional inference architecture. Primary limitations (naive ∀/μ unification, linear substitution) are inherited from the base unifier and are not specific defects of the hole implementation.
